sights.address: SW 152nd St (across from Zoo Miami), Miami, FL
sights.w: 50-acre rail museum across from Zoo Miami — home of the Ferdinand Magellan, the armoured presidential Pullman used by FDR, Truman, Eisenhower and Reagan; train rides and Florida's largest public model railroad.
'Living' aviation museum at the Kendall-Tamiami airport — warbirds that still fly, including a B-26 from the Bay of Pigs invasion.
The original 1936 Parrot Jungle site, now a municipal botanical garden — strangler figs, cypress slough, koi, Swan Lake and the old jungle trails.

sights.address: Hialeah, FL (unincorporated Miami-Dade, north of Hialeah)
sights.w: 515-acre Hialeah park on the old naval air station Earhart flew from — five lakes, the Miami Watersports Complex wakeboard cable, farm village and mountain-bike trails.
Open-air waterfront market on Biscayne Bay — live music daily, bay-cruise docks and the downtown skyline.
18-acre tropical zoological park on Watson Island — the successor to Parrot Jungle, with sloths, lemurs, flamingos and macaws.
Haitian arts centre with galleries, a 300-seat theatre, the Saturday Caribbean Marketplace and the monthly Big Night in Little Haiti Kreyòl concerts.

sights.address: Las Olas Blvd, Fort Lauderdale, FL
sights.w: Broward's flagship art museum on Las Olas — 7,500+ works incl. the largest US collection of CoBrA art and William Glackens; free first Thursdays.
Interactive children's art museum with immersive galleries, now inside Broward Mall in Plantation.
10-acre turn-of-the-century railroad workers' village in Goulds — tropical gardens, antique shops, galleries, tearoom and an aviary.
County marina on Biscayne Bay — gateway to Biscayne NP's keys, with the Biscayne Trail loop and a 1.5-mile jetty walk.
270 acres of pineland next to Zoo Miami — the county's biggest campground, a swimming lake with a seasonal beach and water slide, bridle trails.
Miami's oldest institution still on its original site — the 1924 Mediterranean Revival Jesuit church designed by Owen Williams of Palm Beach.

sights.address: 1821 SW 9th St, Little Havana, Miami, FL
sights.w: Veterans' museum of the 1961 invasion — its prize is the Brigade 2506 flag JFK held up at the Orange Bowl in 1962.

sights.n: American Museum of the Cuban Diaspora
sights.w: 'The Cuban' — exhibitions on the exile experience and Cuban-American art, in a 1930s Coral Way building.

sights.address: Calle Ocho (SW 8th St), Little Havana, Miami, FL
sights.w: Roberto Ramos's museum-bar: one of the largest private collections of pre-revolutionary Cuban art, 480 rums and live son after 8pm.
T.V. Moore's 1920s furniture building — atrium hung with Zaha Hadid's 'Elastika'; Bottura's Torno Subito upstairs.

sights.address: Allapattah (opposite the Rubell Museum), Miami, FL
sights.w: 50,000 sq ft of immersive art — teamLab, James Turrell, Es Devlin rooms that respond to movement and sound.
Artist-founded nonprofit space (25 years in 2026) for site-specific, experimental installations — free.
Two decades of Haitian art, artifacts, music and film in the Design District.

sights.address: 17th St (Lincoln Road area), Miami Beach, FL
sights.w: Frank Gehry's home for the New World Symphony — free WALLCAST concerts and SoundScape Cinema projected on the façade over the park lawn.

sights.address: Ocean Dr at 11th St, Miami Beach, FL
sights.w: The 1930 Mediterranean mansion Gianni Versace made famous — now a hotel and restaurant on Ocean Drive.

sights.address: Main Park Road, Everglades National Park, FL
sights.w: 22+ miles of connected pineland trails west to Pine Glades Lake, plus the park's 108-site east-side campground and fishing pond.

sights.address: Main Park Road (2 mi west of Long Pine Key), Everglades National Park, FL
sights.w: Paved, wheelchair-accessible 0.4-mile loop through slash pine, palmetto and wildflowers over exposed limestone.

sights.address: Main Park Road, Everglades National Park, FL
sights.w: Roadside pond and paddling launch — a wading-bird rookery in nesting season (wood storks, roseate spoonbills).
Half-mile loop round a freshwater pond by Flamingo — wading birds, ducks, alligators and softshell turtles.
